newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines urges free polls in Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Philippines urges free polls in Cambodia.

text.p: The Philippines on Monday urged Cambodia to hold free and fair elections as scheduled and said it looked forward to its eventual membership of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).

President Fidel Ramos made the call in a statement after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said in Phnom Pehn that Cambodia might withdraw its application to join ASEAN if the grouping continued to interfere in Cambodian affairs.
Ramos called on all political parties in Cambodia to preserve the gains the country had achieved under the Paris peace accords and protect the nation's constitution and coalition government.
"It is equally important that free and fair national elections be held on schedule," he added. "The Philippines looks forward to the eventual admission of Cambodia (to ASEAN)."
Cambodia was to join ASEAN this month but the group last week agreed to postpone its entry after Hun Sen ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh from the government.
ASEAN, which groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam, said it would push through with its plan to take in Burma and Laos as new members this month.
